findings.recommendation: Break the cycle by reversing one dependency, introducing an event, or extracting shared responsibility into an owning service. Prioritize two-service cycles because they most directly block independent deployment.

recommendations.architectural_consequence: The cycle blocks independent deployment, increases change coordination, and can turn microservices into a distributed monolith.
recommendations.expected_impact: Improves deployment independence and reduces cascading change risk.
refactoring_steps: Identify the dependency edge in the cycle with the weakest ownership justification.
Reverse that dependency, replace it with an event, or introduce an orchestration/application service.
Move shared domain logic into the service that owns the lifecycle of the data or workflow.
Re-run cycle detection and confirm the cycle is removed.
recommendations.root_cause: The affected services depend on each other directly, usually because ownership of a workflow or domain concept is split across service boundaries.
